source_units.text: At the beginning of the reign of King Jehoiakim son of Josiah, this word came from the Lord:

Thus said the Lord: Stand in the courtyard of the Lord’s house and deliver an oracle to all the Judeans and all who come to bow down in the Lord’s house—all the words I commanded you to deliver to them. Do not take away a word.
Perhaps they will hear and turn, each from his evil way, and I will cease from the evils I plan to do to them because of their evil practices.
And say: Thus said the Lord: If you do not hear Me, walking in My ordinances that I set before your face,
listening to the words of My servants the prophets whom I send to you from early morning, and have sent—though you did not listen to Me—
then I will make this house like Shiloh and make the city a curse to all the nations of all the earth.
And the priests, false prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the Lord’s house.
And when Jeremiah stopped speaking everything the Lord commanded him to speak to all the people, the priests, false prophets, and all the people seized him, saying: You must die!
Because you prophesied in the Lord’s name, saying, This house will be like Shiloh and this city will be emptied of inhabitants. And all the people assembled against Jeremiah in the Lord’s house.
And Judah’s rulers heard this word and went up from the king’s house to the Lord’s house. They sat before the Lord’s New Gate.
And the priests and false prophets said to the rulers and all the people: A sentence of death for this man, because he prophesied against this city, as you heard with your own ears!
And Jeremiah said to the rulers and all the people: The Lord sent me to prophesy against this house and this city all these words you heard.
And now make your ways and works better and hear the Lord’s voice, and the Lord will cease from the evils He spoke against you.
And behold, I am in your hands. Do to me what is advantageous and better for you.
But know for certain that if you kill me, you place innocent blood upon yourselves, this city, and its inhabitants, because the Lord truly sent me to you to speak all these words in your ears.
And the rulers and all the people said to the priests and false prophets: There is no sentence of death for this man, because he spoke to us in the name of the Lord our God.
And men from the land’s elders rose and said to the whole congregation of the people:

Micah the Morathite lived in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah and said to all Judah’s people: Thus said the Lord: Zion will be plowed as a field, Jerusalem will become an untrodden place, and the house’s mountain a grove of woodland.

Did Hezekiah and all Judah kill him? Was it not that they feared the Lord and entreated the Lord’s face, and the Lord ceased from the evils He spoke against them? And we have done great evils against our own lives!
And there was a man prophesying in the Lord’s name, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim. He prophesied concerning this land according to all Jeremiah’s words.
And King Jehoiakim and all the rulers heard all his words and sought to kill him. Uriah heard and entered Egypt.
And the king sent men to Egypt,
and they brought him out from there and brought him to the king. He struck him with the sword and threw him into the tomb of the sons of his people.
Nevertheless, Ahikam son of Shaphan’s hand was with Jeremiah, so that he was not handed into the people’s hands and they did not kill him.
Thus said the Lord: Make bonds and neck collars and put them around your neck,
and send them to Idumea’s king, Moab’s king, the king of Ammon’s sons, Tyre’s king, and Sidon’s king by their messengers coming to meet them in Jerusalem, to Zedekiah king of Judah.
And command them to tell their masters: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Say this to your masters:
I made the earth by My great strength and My lofty undertaking, and I will give it to whoever seems right in My eyes.
I gave the earth to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to serve him, and the field’s beasts to work for him.
And the nation and kingdom, whoever will not put their neck under Babylon’s king’s yoke—I will visit them with sword and famine, said the Lord, until they disappear by his hand.
And do not listen to your false prophets, those divining for you, those dreaming for you, your omens, or your enchantments, who say: You will certainly not work for Babylon’s king.
Because they prophesy false things to you, to remove you far from your land.
And the nation that brings its neck under Babylon’s king’s yoke and works for him, I will leave it in its own land, and it works for him and will dwell in it.
And I spoke to Zedekiah king of Judah according to all these words, saying: Bring your neck,
and work for Babylon’s king, because they prophesy unjust things to you.
Because I did not send them, says the Lord, and they prophesy unjustly in My name to destroy you. You will perish, you and your prophets who prophesy false things unjustly to you.

I spoke to you, all this people, and the priests, saying: Thus said the Lord: Do not listen to the prophets’ words prophesying to you, Behold, the vessels of the Lord’s house will return from Babylon, because they prophesy unjust things to you. I did not send them.
If they are prophets and the Lord’s word is in them, let them meet with Me.
Because thus said the Lord: And of the remaining vessels,
which Babylon’s king did not take when he deported Jeconiah from Jerusalem,
they will go into Babylon, says the Lord.
And in the fourth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fifth month, Hananiah son of Azzur, the false prophet from Gibeon, said to me in the Lord’s house before the priests and all the people:
Thus said the Lord: I smashed Babylon’s king’s yoke.
In two full years I will return to this place the vessels of the Lord’s house,
and Jeconiah and Judah’s deportees, because I will smash Babylon’s king’s yoke.
And Jeremiah said to Hananiah before all the people and before the priests standing in the Lord’s house,
and Jeremiah said: Truly! May the Lord do so. May He establish your word that you prophesy, returning the vessels of the Lord’s house and all the deportees from Babylon to this place.
Nevertheless, hear the Lord’s word that I speak in your ears and in all the people’s ears:
The prophets who were before me and before you from of old prophesied over much land and against great kingdoms concerning war.
The prophet who prophesied peace—when the word comes, they will know the prophet whom the Lord sent to them in faithfulness.
And Hananiah took the collars from Jeremiah’s neck before all the people and smashed them.
And Hananiah said before all the people: Thus said the Lord: This is how I will smash Babylon’s king’s yoke from all the nations’ necks. And Jeremiah went his way.
And the Lord’s word came to Jeremiah after Hananiah smashed the collars from his neck, saying:
Go and tell Hananiah: Thus said the Lord: You smashed wooden collars, and I will make iron collars in their place.
Because thus said the Lord: I placed an iron yoke upon all the nations’ necks to work for Babylon’s king.
And Jeremiah said to Hananiah: The Lord has not sent you, and you made this people trust in injustice.
Therefore thus said the Lord: Behold, I am sending you away from the earth’s face. This year you will die.
And he died in the seventh month.
And these are the words of the document Jeremiah sent from Jerusalem to the elders of the deportation, the priests, and the false prophets—a letter to Babylon for the deportees and all the people—
after King Jeconiah, the queen, the eunuchs, and every free person, prisoner, and craftsman left Jerusalem,
by Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Babylon’s king in Babylon, saying:
Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God, concerning the deportees whom I deported from Jerusalem:
Build houses and dwell in them; plant gardens and eat their fruits,
and take wives and beget sons and daughters. Take wives for your sons and give your daughters to husbands. Multiply and do not become fewer,
and seek the peace of the land where I deported you, and pray to the Lord for them, because in its peace you will have peace.
Because thus said the Lord: Do not let the false prophets among you persuade you, and do not let your diviners persuade you. Do not listen to your dreams that you dream,
because they prophesy unjust things to you in My name, and I did not send them.
Because thus said the Lord: When seventy years are about to be fulfilled for Babylon, I will visit you and establish My words for you, to return your people to this place.
And I will plan for you a plan of peace and not evils, to give you these things.
And pray to Me, and I will listen to you.
And seek Me earnestly, and you will find Me, because you will seek Me with your whole heart,
and I will appear to you.
Because you said: The Lord established prophets for us in Babylon,
Thus said the Lord concerning Ahab and Zedekiah: Behold, I am giving them into Babylon’s king’s hands, and he will strike them before your eyes.
And all Judah’s deportees in Babylon will take a curse from them, saying: May the Lord make you as He made Zedekiah and Ahab, whom Babylon’s king fried in fire,

because of the lawlessness they committed in Israel: they committed adultery with their fellow citizens’ wives and delivered an oracle in My name that I did not command them. I am a witness, says the Lord.
And to Shemaiah the Nelamite say:
I did not send you in My name. And to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest say:

The Lord appointed you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to become an overseer in the Lord’s house over every person prophesying and every person raging, and you will put him into confinement and into the trap.
And now why did you join in reviling Jeremiah from Anathoth, who prophesied to you?
Was it not for this that he sent to you in Babylon, saying: It is far off. Build houses and dwell in them; plant gardens, and you will eat their fruit?
And Zephaniah read the document in Jeremiah’s hearing.
And the Lord’s word came to Jeremiah, saying:
Send to the deportees, saying: Thus said the Lord concerning Shemaiah the Nelamite: Since Shemaiah prophesied to you, though I did not send him, and made you trust in unjust things,
therefore thus said the Lord: Behold, I will visit Shemaiah and his family, and none of them will be among you to see the good things I will do for you. They will not see.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Write in a book all the words I delivered to you as oracles,

because behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will return the deportees of My people Israel and Judah, said the Lord. I will return them to the land I gave their fathers, and they will rule over it.
And these are the words the Lord spoke concerning Israel and Judah:
Thus said the Lord: You will hear a sound of fear—fear, and there is no peace.
Ask and see whether a male gave birth, and about fear in which they will hold loins and salvation. For I have seen every person with his hands upon his loins; faces turned toward jaundice—
so it became. For that day is great, and there is none like it; it is a narrow time for Jacob, and he will be saved from it.
On that day, said the Lord, I will smash the yoke from their neck and tear apart their bonds, and they will no longer work for foreigners.
And they will work for the Lord their God, and I will raise up David their king for them.
Thus said the Lord: I raised up a fracture; your wound is painful.
There is no one judging your case; you were treated into pain. There is no benefit for you.
All your friends forgot you; they will certainly not inquire. For I struck you with an enemy’s blow, a firm discipline; upon all your injustice your sins multiplied.

Therefore all who eat you will be eaten; as for all your enemies, they will eat all their flesh. Upon the multitude of your injustices your sins multiplied; they did these things to you. Those plundering you will become plunder, and I will give all who despoil you as spoil.
Because I will bring up your cure and heal you from a painful wound, says the Lord, because you were called Scattered: She is your prey, because no one seeks her.
Thus said the Lord: Behold, I will return Jacob’s deportees and have mercy on his captivity. A city will be built upon its height, and the sanctuary will sit according to its judgment.
And singers and the sound of people playing will come out from them. I will increase them, and they will certainly not be diminished.
And their sons will enter as formerly, and their testimonies will be set upright before Me. I will visit those afflicting them.
And stronger ones of his will be over them, and his ruler will come out from him. I will gather them, and they will return to Me. For who is this who gave his heart to return to Me? says the Lord.
Because the Lord’s anger went out furious; swirling anger went out and will come upon the ungodly.
The anger of the Lord’s fury will certainly not turn back until He acts and establishes His heart’s undertaking. At the end of the days you will know these things.
At that time, said the Lord, I will be God to Israel’s family, and they will be My people.
Thus said the Lord: I found warmth in the wilderness among those who perished by the sword. Go, and do not destroy Israel.
The Lord appeared to him from afar: I loved you with an eternal love; therefore I drew you into compassion.
Again I will build you, and you will be built, virgin Israel. Again you will take your tambourine and go out with a gathering of people playing.
Again plant vineyards on Samaria’s mountains; plant and praise.
Because there is a day of calling by those making their defense in Ephraim’s mountains: Rise and go up to Zion, to the Lord our God.
Because thus said the Lord to Jacob: Rejoice and neigh aloud toward the head of the nations; make it heard and praise. Say: The Lord saved His people, Israel’s remnant!
Behold, I am bringing them from the north and will gather them from the earth’s farthest end at the Passover festival. You will bear a great crowd, and they will return here.

They went out with weeping, and with encouragement I will bring them up, lodging them beside water channels on a straight road where they will certainly not wander, because I became Israel’s father, and Ephraim is My firstborn.
Hear the Lord’s word, nations, and announce it to the farther islands. Say: He who winnowed Israel will gather him and guard him like one tending his flock.
Because the Lord ransomed Jacob and rescued him from the hand of those stronger than he.

They will come and rejoice on Mount Zion; they will come for the Lord’s good things, to a land of grain, wine, fruits, livestock, and sheep. Their life will be like a fruitful tree, and they will hunger no more.
Then virgins will rejoice in a gathering of young men, and elders will rejoice. I will turn their mourning into gladness and make them joyful.
I will magnify and fill the priests’ souls to abundance, the sons of Levi, and My people will be filled with My good things.
Thus said the Lord: A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, weeping, and wailing. Rachel, weeping aloud, would not stop over her sons, because they are no more.
Thus said the Lord: Let your voice cease from weeping and your eyes from your tears, because your works have a reward, and they will return from enemies’ land,
a lasting stay for your children.
I surely heard Ephraim wailing: Thou didst discipline me, and I was disciplined; like a calf I was not taught. Turn me back, and I will return, because Thou art the Lord my God.
Because after my captivity I repented, and after I came to know, I groaned over days of shame and showed Thee that I received reproach from my youth.
Ephraim is a beloved son to Me, a child taking delight, because My words are in him; I will surely remember him. Therefore I hastened toward him; I will surely have mercy on him, says the Lord.
Stand firm, Zion; carry out punishment; set your heart upon the shoulders. Turn back along the road you traveled, virgin Israel; turn back to your cities in mourning.
How long will you turn away, dishonored daughter? Because the Lord created salvation for a new planting; people will go about in salvation.
Thus said the Lord: They will again say this word in Judah’s land and its cities when I return its captivity: Blessed is the Lord over the righteous mountain, His holy mountain,
and those dwelling in Judah’s cities and all its land together with a farmer; and he will be lifted up with a flock.
Because I filled every thirsty soul to abundance and filled every hungry soul.
Therefore I awoke and saw, and my sleep became sweet to me.
Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will sow Israel and Judah with human seed and livestock seed.
And just as I watched over them to tear down and harm, so I will watch over them to build and plant, says the Lord.
In those days they will certainly not say: The fathers ate an unripe grape, and the children’s teeth were set on edge.
Instead, each will die in his own sin, and the one eating the unripe grape will have his own teeth set on edge.
Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,

not according to the covenant I made with their fathers on the day I took their hand to bring them out of Egypt’s land, because they did not remain in My covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.

Because this is the covenant I will make with Israel’s house after those days, says the Lord: I will surely put My laws into their understanding and write them upon their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be My people.

And they will certainly not teach each his fellow citizen or his brother, saying, Know the Lord, because they will all know Me, from their least to their greatest. I will be merciful toward their injustices and certainly remember their sins no more.
If the heaven is raised to the height, says the Lord, and the earth’s ground lowered beneath, even then I do not reject Israel’s family, says the Lord, for all they did.
Thus said the Lord, who gave the sun for daylight, moon and stars for night light, and a cry in the sea so its waves boomed—the Lord Almighty is His name:
If these laws cease from before Me, says the Lord, then Israel’s family will cease to be a nation before Me for all days.
Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and a city will be built for the Lord from Hanamel’s tower to the Corner Gate.
And its measurement will go out opposite them as far as Gareb’s hills, and it will be enclosed all around with chosen stones.
And all Asaremoth as far as the Kidron wadi, to the corner of the eastern Horse Gate, will be a sanctuary for the Lord. It will certainly never disappear or be torn down for ever.
The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah in King Zedekiah’s tenth year, which was the eighteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
The king of Babylon’s force had built siegeworks against Jerusalem, and Jeremiah was kept in the prison court at the king’s house.
King Zedekiah had shut him in there, saying, Why do you prophesy, saying, Thus said the Lord: I am handing this city over to Babylon’s king, and he will take it?
Zedekiah will certainly not be saved from the Chaldeans’ hand, but will certainly be handed over to Babylon’s king. His mouth will speak to his mouth, and his eyes will see his eyes.
Zedekiah will enter Babylon and remain there.
The Lord’s word came to Jeremiah:
Hanamel son of Shallum, your father’s brother, is coming to you, saying, Acquire my field at Anathoth for yourself, because you have the right to receive it as a possession.

Hanamel son of Shallum, my father’s brother, came to me in the prison court and said, Acquire my field in Benjamin’s land at Anathoth, because you have the right to acquire it, and you are the elder. Then I knew that this was the Lord’s word.
I acquired the field of Hanamel, my father’s brother’s son, and weighed out to him seventeen shekels of silver.
I wrote a document, sealed it, called witnesses, and weighed the silver on a balance.
I took the purchase document, the sealed one and the one that had been read.

I gave it to Baruch son of Neriah son of Maaseiah, before Hanamel my father’s brother’s son, before those standing there and writing in the purchase document, and before the Judeans in the prison court.
Before their eyes I instructed Baruch:
Thus said the Lord Almighty: Take this purchase document and the document that has been read, and put it in an earthenware vessel so that it may last many days.
For thus said the Lord: Fields, houses, and vineyards will again be acquired in this land.
After giving the purchase document to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the Lord:
O Lord, Thou madest heaven and earth by Thy great strength and Thy high, uplifted arm. Nothing can be hidden from Thee.
Thou showest mercy to thousands and repayest fathers’ sins into their children’s laps after them, the great and strong God,
Lord of great counsel and powerful in works, the great God, the Almighty and renowned Lord. Thine eyes are upon the ways of human beings, to give each according to his way.
Thou didst perform signs and wonders in Egypt down to this day, in Israel and among earthborn people, and madest a name for Thyself as it is this day.
Thou broughtest Thy people Israel out of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a mighty hand, a high arm, and great sights.
Thou gavest them this land, which Thou hadst sworn to their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.
They entered and received it, but did not obey Thy voice or walk in Thine ordinances. They did none of all that Thou didst command them, and Thou didst cause all these calamities to befall them.
A multitude has reached this city to seize it. The city was handed over to the Chaldeans fighting it because of sword and famine. As Thou spakest, so it happened.
Yet Thou sayest to me, Acquire a field with silver. And I wrote a document, sealed it, and called witnesses—even though the city was handed over to the Chaldeans.
The Lord’s word came to me:
I am the Lord, the God of all flesh. Can anything be hidden from Me?
Therefore thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: This city will certainly be handed over to Babylon’s king, and he will take it.

The Chaldeans fighting this city will come and burn this city with fire. They will burn down the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to Baal and poured libations to other gods to provoke Me bitterly.
The children of Israel and Judah alone were doing evil in My sight from their youth.
This city has aroused My anger and wrath from the day they built it until this day, so that I would remove it from My presence,

because of all the wicked deeds the children of Israel and Judah committed to embitter Me—they and their kings, their rulers, their priests, their prophets, the men of Judah and Jerusalem’s inhabitants.
They turned their backs to Me, not their faces. I taught them from early morning and kept teaching, but they did not listen and take hold of discipline.
They set their pollutions in the house over which My name is invoked, amid their impurities.

They built the altars to Baal in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, to offer their sons and daughters to Molech the king. I had not instructed them, nor had it entered My heart, to do this abomination and cause Judah to sin.
And now, thus said the Lord, Israel’s God, concerning the city of which you say, It will be handed over to Babylon’s king by sword, famine, and a sent affliction:
I am gathering them from all the land where I scattered them in My anger, wrath, and great indignation. I will bring them back to this place and settle them in confidence.
They will be My people, and I will be their God.
I will give them another way and another heart, to fear Me always, for their good and their children’s good after them.
I will establish an eternal covenant with them, which I will certainly not turn back from behind them. I will put My fear in their heart so that they do not depart from Me.
I will attend to them to do them good and will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all heart and all soul.
For thus said the Lord: Just as I brought all these great calamities upon this people, so I will bring upon them all the good things I spoke concerning them.
Fields will again be acquired in the land of which you say, It is untrodden by people and animals, and they were handed over to the Chaldeans.

They will acquire fields with silver, and you will write a document, seal it, and call witnesses in Benjamin’s land, around Jerusalem, in Judah’s cities, the hill-country cities, the cities of the Shephelah, and the cities of the Negeb, because I will bring back their exiles.
The Lord’s word came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still bound in the prison court:
Thus said the Lord, who makes the earth and forms it to set it upright—the Lord is His name:
Cry out to Me and I will answer you. I will announce to you great, mighty things you have not known.
For thus said the Lord, Israel’s God, about this city’s houses and the houses of Judah’s king, torn down for siegeworks and defenses,
to fight the Chaldeans and fill the city with the dead bodies of people I struck in My anger and wrath. I turned My face from them because of all their wicked deeds.
I am bringing her the closing of wounds and a remedy. I will reveal to them that I listen, heal her, and make peace and faithfulness for them.
I will bring back Judah’s exiles and Israel’s exiles and build them as before.
I will cleanse them from all the injustices by which they sinned against Me. I will certainly not remember the sins they committed against Me when they departed from Me.

It will be for joy, praise, and greatness to all the people of the earth. They will hear all the good things I will do, and they will fear and be distressed over all the good and peace I will bring them.
Thus said the Lord: Again in this place, which you call deserted of people and animals, in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem, desolate because there are no people or animals, there will be heard

the sound of joy and rejoicing, the bridegroom’s voice and the bride’s voice, the voices of those saying, Give thanks to the Lord Almighty, for the Lord is good; His mercy is for ever. They will bring gifts into the Lord’s house, for I will bring back all the exiles of that land as before, said the Lord.
Thus said the Lord of forces: Again in this place, deserted because there are no people or animals, and in all its cities, there will be lodgings for shepherds settling sheep down.

In the hill-country cities, the cities of the Shephelah, the cities of the Negeb, in Benjamin’s land, in the places around Jerusalem, and in Judah’s cities, sheep will again pass under the hand of the one counting, said the Lord.

Jeremiah 33:1.text: At the beginning of the reign of King Jehoiakim son of Josiah, this word came from the Lord:

Jeremiah 33:2.text: Thus said the Lord: Stand in the courtyard of the Lord’s house and deliver an oracle to all the Judeans and all who come to bow down in the Lord’s house—all the words I commanded you to deliver to them. Do not take away a word.

Jeremiah 33:3.text: Perhaps they will hear and turn, each from his evil way, and I will cease from the evils I plan to do to them because of their evil practices.

Jeremiah 33:4.text: And say: Thus said the Lord: If you do not hear Me, walking in My ordinances that I set before your face,

Jeremiah 33:5.text: listening to the words of My servants the prophets whom I send to you from early morning, and have sent—though you did not listen to Me—

Jeremiah 33:6.text: then I will make this house like Shiloh and make the city a curse to all the nations of all the earth.

Jeremiah 33:7.text: And the priests, false prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the Lord’s house.

Jeremiah 33:8.text: And when Jeremiah stopped speaking everything the Lord commanded him to speak to all the people, the priests, false prophets, and all the people seized him, saying: You must die!

Jeremiah 33:9.text: Because you prophesied in the Lord’s name, saying, This house will be like Shiloh and this city will be emptied of inhabitants. And all the people assembled against Jeremiah in the Lord’s house.

Jeremiah 33:10.text: And Judah’s rulers heard this word and went up from the king’s house to the Lord’s house. They sat before the Lord’s New Gate.

Jeremiah 33:11.text: And the priests and false prophets said to the rulers and all the people: A sentence of death for this man, because he prophesied against this city, as you heard with your own ears!

Jeremiah 33:12.text: And Jeremiah said to the rulers and all the people: The Lord sent me to prophesy against this house and this city all these words you heard.

Jeremiah 33:13.text: And now make your ways and works better and hear the Lord’s voice, and the Lord will cease from the evils He spoke against you.

Jeremiah 33:14.text: And behold, I am in your hands. Do to me what is advantageous and better for you.

Jeremiah 33:15.text: But know for certain that if you kill me, you place innocent blood upon yourselves, this city, and its inhabitants, because the Lord truly sent me to you to speak all these words in your ears.

Jeremiah 33:16.text: And the rulers and all the people said to the priests and false prophets: There is no sentence of death for this man, because he spoke to us in the name of the Lord our God.

Jeremiah 33:17.text: And men from the land’s elders rose and said to the whole congregation of the people:

Jeremiah 33:18.text: Micah the Morathite lived in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah and said to all Judah’s people: Thus said the Lord: Zion will be plowed as a field, Jerusalem will become an untrodden place, and the house’s mountain a grove of woodland.

Jeremiah 33:19.text: Did Hezekiah and all Judah kill him? Was it not that they feared the Lord and entreated the Lord’s face, and the Lord ceased from the evils He spoke against them? And we have done great evils against our own lives!

Jeremiah 33:20.text: And there was a man prophesying in the Lord’s name, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim. He prophesied concerning this land according to all Jeremiah’s words.

Jeremiah 33:21.text: And King Jehoiakim and all the rulers heard all his words and sought to kill him. Uriah heard and entered Egypt.

Jeremiah 33:22.text: And the king sent men to Egypt,

Jeremiah 33:23.text: and they brought him out from there and brought him to the king. He struck him with the sword and threw him into the tomb of the sons of his people.

Jeremiah 33:24.text: Nevertheless, Ahikam son of Shaphan’s hand was with Jeremiah, so that he was not handed into the people’s hands and they did not kill him.

Jeremiah 34:2.text: Thus said the Lord: Make bonds and neck collars and put them around your neck,

Jeremiah 34:3.text: and send them to Idumea’s king, Moab’s king, the king of Ammon’s sons, Tyre’s king, and Sidon’s king by their messengers coming to meet them in Jerusalem, to Zedekiah king of Judah.

Jeremiah 34:4.text: And command them to tell their masters: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Say this to your masters:

Jeremiah 34:5.text: I made the earth by My great strength and My lofty undertaking, and I will give it to whoever seems right in My eyes.

Jeremiah 34:6.text: I gave the earth to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to serve him, and the field’s beasts to work for him.

Jeremiah 34:8.text: And the nation and kingdom, whoever will not put their neck under Babylon’s king’s yoke—I will visit them with sword and famine, said the Lord, until they disappear by his hand.

Jeremiah 34:9.text: And do not listen to your false prophets, those divining for you, those dreaming for you, your omens, or your enchantments, who say: You will certainly not work for Babylon’s king.

Jeremiah 34:10.text: Because they prophesy false things to you, to remove you far from your land.

Jeremiah 34:11.text: And the nation that brings its neck under Babylon’s king’s yoke and works for him, I will leave it in its own land, and it works for him and will dwell in it.

Jeremiah 34:12.text: And I spoke to Zedekiah king of Judah according to all these words, saying: Bring your neck,

Jeremiah 34:14.text: and work for Babylon’s king, because they prophesy unjust things to you.

Jeremiah 34:15.text: Because I did not send them, says the Lord, and they prophesy unjustly in My name to destroy you. You will perish, you and your prophets who prophesy false things unjustly to you.

Jeremiah 34:16.text: I spoke to you, all this people, and the priests, saying: Thus said the Lord: Do not listen to the prophets’ words prophesying to you, Behold, the vessels of the Lord’s house will return from Babylon, because they prophesy unjust things to you. I did not send them.

Jeremiah 34:18.text: If they are prophets and the Lord’s word is in them, let them meet with Me.

Jeremiah 34:19.text: Because thus said the Lord: And of the remaining vessels,

Jeremiah 34:20.text: which Babylon’s king did not take when he deported Jeconiah from Jerusalem,

Jeremiah 34:22.text: they will go into Babylon, says the Lord.

Jeremiah 35:1.text: And in the fourth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fifth month, Hananiah son of Azzur, the false prophet from Gibeon, said to me in the Lord’s house before the priests and all the people:

Jeremiah 35:2.text: Thus said the Lord: I smashed Babylon’s king’s yoke.

Jeremiah 35:3.text: In two full years I will return to this place the vessels of the Lord’s house,

Jeremiah 35:4.text: and Jeconiah and Judah’s deportees, because I will smash Babylon’s king’s yoke.

Jeremiah 35:5.text: And Jeremiah said to Hananiah before all the people and before the priests standing in the Lord’s house,

Jeremiah 35:6.text: and Jeremiah said: Truly! May the Lord do so. May He establish your word that you prophesy, returning the vessels of the Lord’s house and all the deportees from Babylon to this place.

Jeremiah 35:7.text: Nevertheless, hear the Lord’s word that I speak in your ears and in all the people’s ears:

Jeremiah 35:8.text: The prophets who were before me and before you from of old prophesied over much land and against great kingdoms concerning war.

Jeremiah 35:9.text: The prophet who prophesied peace—when the word comes, they will know the prophet whom the Lord sent to them in faithfulness.

Jeremiah 35:10.text: And Hananiah took the collars from Jeremiah’s neck before all the people and smashed them.

Jeremiah 35:11.text: And Hananiah said before all the people: Thus said the Lord: This is how I will smash Babylon’s king’s yoke from all the nations’ necks. And Jeremiah went his way.

Jeremiah 35:12.text: And the Lord’s word came to Jeremiah after Hananiah smashed the collars from his neck, saying:

Jeremiah 35:13.text: Go and tell Hananiah: Thus said the Lord: You smashed wooden collars, and I will make iron collars in their place.

Jeremiah 35:14.text: Because thus said the Lord: I placed an iron yoke upon all the nations’ necks to work for Babylon’s king.

Jeremiah 35:15.text: And Jeremiah said to Hananiah: The Lord has not sent you, and you made this people trust in injustice.

Jeremiah 35:16.text: Therefore thus said the Lord: Behold, I am sending you away from the earth’s face. This year you will die.

Jeremiah 35:17.text: And he died in the seventh month.

Jeremiah 36:1.text: And these are the words of the document Jeremiah sent from Jerusalem to the elders of the deportation, the priests, and the false prophets—a letter to Babylon for the deportees and all the people—

Jeremiah 36:2.text: after King Jeconiah, the queen, the eunuchs, and every free person, prisoner, and craftsman left Jerusalem,

Jeremiah 36:3.text: by Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Babylon’s king in Babylon, saying:

Jeremiah 36:4.text: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God, concerning the deportees whom I deported from Jerusalem:

Jeremiah 36:5.text: Build houses and dwell in them; plant gardens and eat their fruits,

Jeremiah 36:6.text: and take wives and beget sons and daughters. Take wives for your sons and give your daughters to husbands. Multiply and do not become fewer,

Jeremiah 36:7.text: and seek the peace of the land where I deported you, and pray to the Lord for them, because in its peace you will have peace.

Jeremiah 36:8.text: Because thus said the Lord: Do not let the false prophets among you persuade you, and do not let your diviners persuade you. Do not listen to your dreams that you dream,

Jeremiah 36:9.text: because they prophesy unjust things to you in My name, and I did not send them.

Jeremiah 36:10.text: Because thus said the Lord: When seventy years are about to be fulfilled for Babylon, I will visit you and establish My words for you, to return your people to this place.

Jeremiah 36:11.text: And I will plan for you a plan of peace and not evils, to give you these things.

Jeremiah 36:12.text: And pray to Me, and I will listen to you.

Jeremiah 36:13.text: And seek Me earnestly, and you will find Me, because you will seek Me with your whole heart,

Jeremiah 36:14.text: and I will appear to you.

Jeremiah 36:15.text: Because you said: The Lord established prophets for us in Babylon,

Jeremiah 36:21.text: Thus said the Lord concerning Ahab and Zedekiah: Behold, I am giving them into Babylon’s king’s hands, and he will strike them before your eyes.

Jeremiah 36:22.text: And all Judah’s deportees in Babylon will take a curse from them, saying: May the Lord make you as He made Zedekiah and Ahab, whom Babylon’s king fried in fire,

Jeremiah 36:23.text: because of the lawlessness they committed in Israel: they committed adultery with their fellow citizens’ wives and delivered an oracle in My name that I did not command them. I am a witness, says the Lord.

Jeremiah 36:24.text: And to Shemaiah the Nelamite say:

Jeremiah 36:25.text: I did not send you in My name. And to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest say:

Jeremiah 36:26.text: The Lord appointed you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to become an overseer in the Lord’s house over every person prophesying and every person raging, and you will put him into confinement and into the trap.

Jeremiah 36:27.text: And now why did you join in reviling Jeremiah from Anathoth, who prophesied to you?

Jeremiah 36:28.text: Was it not for this that he sent to you in Babylon, saying: It is far off. Build houses and dwell in them; plant gardens, and you will eat their fruit?

Jeremiah 36:29.text: And Zephaniah read the document in Jeremiah’s hearing.

Jeremiah 36:30.text: And the Lord’s word came to Jeremiah, saying:

Jeremiah 36:31.text: Send to the deportees, saying: Thus said the Lord concerning Shemaiah the Nelamite: Since Shemaiah prophesied to you, though I did not send him, and made you trust in unjust things,

Jeremiah 36:32.text: therefore thus said the Lord: Behold, I will visit Shemaiah and his family, and none of them will be among you to see the good things I will do for you. They will not see.

Jeremiah 37:1.text: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:

Jeremiah 37:2.text: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Write in a book all the words I delivered to you as oracles,

Jeremiah 37:3.text: because behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will return the deportees of My people Israel and Judah, said the Lord. I will return them to the land I gave their fathers, and they will rule over it.

Jeremiah 37:4.text: And these are the words the Lord spoke concerning Israel and Judah:

Jeremiah 37:5.text: Thus said the Lord: You will hear a sound of fear—fear, and there is no peace.

Jeremiah 37:6.text: Ask and see whether a male gave birth, and about fear in which they will hold loins and salvation. For I have seen every person with his hands upon his loins; faces turned toward jaundice—

Jeremiah 37:7.text: so it became. For that day is great, and there is none like it; it is a narrow time for Jacob, and he will be saved from it.

Jeremiah 37:8.text: On that day, said the Lord, I will smash the yoke from their neck and tear apart their bonds, and they will no longer work for foreigners.

Jeremiah 37:9.text: And they will work for the Lord their God, and I will raise up David their king for them.

Jeremiah 37:12.text: Thus said the Lord: I raised up a fracture; your wound is painful.

Jeremiah 37:13.text: There is no one judging your case; you were treated into pain. There is no benefit for you.

Jeremiah 37:14.text: All your friends forgot you; they will certainly not inquire. For I struck you with an enemy’s blow, a firm discipline; upon all your injustice your sins multiplied.

Jeremiah 37:16.text: Therefore all who eat you will be eaten; as for all your enemies, they will eat all their flesh. Upon the multitude of your injustices your sins multiplied; they did these things to you. Those plundering you will become plunder, and I will give all who despoil you as spoil.

Jeremiah 37:17.text: Because I will bring up your cure and heal you from a painful wound, says the Lord, because you were called Scattered: She is your prey, because no one seeks her.

Jeremiah 37:18.text: Thus said the Lord: Behold, I will return Jacob’s deportees and have mercy on his captivity. A city will be built upon its height, and the sanctuary will sit according to its judgment.

Jeremiah 37:19.text: And singers and the sound of people playing will come out from them. I will increase them, and they will certainly not be diminished.

Jeremiah 37:20.text: And their sons will enter as formerly, and their testimonies will be set upright before Me. I will visit those afflicting them.

Jeremiah 37:21.text: And stronger ones of his will be over them, and his ruler will come out from him. I will gather them, and they will return to Me. For who is this who gave his heart to return to Me? says the Lord.

Jeremiah 37:23.text: Because the Lord’s anger went out furious; swirling anger went out and will come upon the ungodly.

Jeremiah 37:24.text: The anger of the Lord’s fury will certainly not turn back until He acts and establishes His heart’s undertaking. At the end of the days you will know these things.

Jeremiah 38:1.text: At that time, said the Lord, I will be God to Israel’s family, and they will be My people.

Jeremiah 38:2.text: Thus said the Lord: I found warmth in the wilderness among those who perished by the sword. Go, and do not destroy Israel.

Jeremiah 38:3.text: The Lord appeared to him from afar: I loved you with an eternal love; therefore I drew you into compassion.

Jeremiah 38:4.text: Again I will build you, and you will be built, virgin Israel. Again you will take your tambourine and go out with a gathering of people playing.

Jeremiah 38:5.text: Again plant vineyards on Samaria’s mountains; plant and praise.

Jeremiah 38:6.text: Because there is a day of calling by those making their defense in Ephraim’s mountains: Rise and go up to Zion, to the Lord our God.

Jeremiah 38:7.text: Because thus said the Lord to Jacob: Rejoice and neigh aloud toward the head of the nations; make it heard and praise. Say: The Lord saved His people, Israel’s remnant!

Jeremiah 38:8.text: Behold, I am bringing them from the north and will gather them from the earth’s farthest end at the Passover festival. You will bear a great crowd, and they will return here.

Jeremiah 38:9.text: They went out with weeping, and with encouragement I will bring them up, lodging them beside water channels on a straight road where they will certainly not wander, because I became Israel’s father, and Ephraim is My firstborn.

Jeremiah 38:10.text: Hear the Lord’s word, nations, and announce it to the farther islands. Say: He who winnowed Israel will gather him and guard him like one tending his flock.

Jeremiah 38:11.text: Because the Lord ransomed Jacob and rescued him from the hand of those stronger than he.

Jeremiah 38:12.text: They will come and rejoice on Mount Zion; they will come for the Lord’s good things, to a land of grain, wine, fruits, livestock, and sheep. Their life will be like a fruitful tree, and they will hunger no more.

Jeremiah 38:13.text: Then virgins will rejoice in a gathering of young men, and elders will rejoice. I will turn their mourning into gladness and make them joyful.

Jeremiah 38:14.text: I will magnify and fill the priests’ souls to abundance, the sons of Levi, and My people will be filled with My good things.

Jeremiah 38:15.text: Thus said the Lord: A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, weeping, and wailing. Rachel, weeping aloud, would not stop over her sons, because they are no more.

Jeremiah 38:16.text: Thus said the Lord: Let your voice cease from weeping and your eyes from your tears, because your works have a reward, and they will return from enemies’ land,

Jeremiah 38:17.text: a lasting stay for your children.

Jeremiah 38:18.text: I surely heard Ephraim wailing: Thou didst discipline me, and I was disciplined; like a calf I was not taught. Turn me back, and I will return, because Thou art the Lord my God.

Jeremiah 38:19.text: Because after my captivity I repented, and after I came to know, I groaned over days of shame and showed Thee that I received reproach from my youth.

Jeremiah 38:20.text: Ephraim is a beloved son to Me, a child taking delight, because My words are in him; I will surely remember him. Therefore I hastened toward him; I will surely have mercy on him, says the Lord.

Jeremiah 38:21.text: Stand firm, Zion; carry out punishment; set your heart upon the shoulders. Turn back along the road you traveled, virgin Israel; turn back to your cities in mourning.

Jeremiah 38:22.text: How long will you turn away, dishonored daughter? Because the Lord created salvation for a new planting; people will go about in salvation.

Jeremiah 38:23.text: Thus said the Lord: They will again say this word in Judah’s land and its cities when I return its captivity: Blessed is the Lord over the righteous mountain, His holy mountain,

Jeremiah 38:24.text: and those dwelling in Judah’s cities and all its land together with a farmer; and he will be lifted up with a flock.

Jeremiah 38:25.text: Because I filled every thirsty soul to abundance and filled every hungry soul.

Jeremiah 38:26.text: Therefore I awoke and saw, and my sleep became sweet to me.

Jeremiah 38:27.text: Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will sow Israel and Judah with human seed and livestock seed.

Jeremiah 38:28.text: And just as I watched over them to tear down and harm, so I will watch over them to build and plant, says the Lord.

Jeremiah 38:29.text: In those days they will certainly not say: The fathers ate an unripe grape, and the children’s teeth were set on edge.

Jeremiah 38:30.text: Instead, each will die in his own sin, and the one eating the unripe grape will have his own teeth set on edge.

Jeremiah 38:31.text: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,

Jeremiah 38:32.text: not according to the covenant I made with their fathers on the day I took their hand to bring them out of Egypt’s land, because they did not remain in My covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.

Jeremiah 38:33.text: Because this is the covenant I will make with Israel’s house after those days, says the Lord: I will surely put My laws into their understanding and write them upon their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be My people.

Jeremiah 38:34.text: And they will certainly not teach each his fellow citizen or his brother, saying, Know the Lord, because they will all know Me, from their least to their greatest. I will be merciful toward their injustices and certainly remember their sins no more.

Jeremiah 38:35.text: If the heaven is raised to the height, says the Lord, and the earth’s ground lowered beneath, even then I do not reject Israel’s family, says the Lord, for all they did.

Jeremiah 38:36.text: Thus said the Lord, who gave the sun for daylight, moon and stars for night light, and a cry in the sea so its waves boomed—the Lord Almighty is His name:

Jeremiah 38:37.text: If these laws cease from before Me, says the Lord, then Israel’s family will cease to be a nation before Me for all days.

Jeremiah 38:38.text: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and a city will be built for the Lord from Hanamel’s tower to the Corner Gate.

Jeremiah 38:39.text: And its measurement will go out opposite them as far as Gareb’s hills, and it will be enclosed all around with chosen stones.

Jeremiah 38:40.text: And all Asaremoth as far as the Kidron wadi, to the corner of the eastern Horse Gate, will be a sanctuary for the Lord. It will certainly never disappear or be torn down for ever.

Jeremiah 39:1.text: The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah in King Zedekiah’s tenth year, which was the eighteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.

Jeremiah 39:2.text: The king of Babylon’s force had built siegeworks against Jerusalem, and Jeremiah was kept in the prison court at the king’s house.

Jeremiah 39:3.text: King Zedekiah had shut him in there, saying, Why do you prophesy, saying, Thus said the Lord: I am handing this city over to Babylon’s king, and he will take it?

Jeremiah 39:4.text: Zedekiah will certainly not be saved from the Chaldeans’ hand, but will certainly be handed over to Babylon’s king. His mouth will speak to his mouth, and his eyes will see his eyes.

Jeremiah 39:5.text: Zedekiah will enter Babylon and remain there.

Jeremiah 39:6.text: The Lord’s word came to Jeremiah:

Jeremiah 39:7.text: Hanamel son of Shallum, your father’s brother, is coming to you, saying, Acquire my field at Anathoth for yourself, because you have the right to receive it as a possession.

Jeremiah 39:8.text: Hanamel son of Shallum, my father’s brother, came to me in the prison court and said, Acquire my field in Benjamin’s land at Anathoth, because you have the right to acquire it, and you are the elder. Then I knew that this was the Lord’s word.

Jeremiah 39:9.text: I acquired the field of Hanamel, my father’s brother’s son, and weighed out to him seventeen shekels of silver.

Jeremiah 39:10.text: I wrote a document, sealed it, called witnesses, and weighed the silver on a balance.

Jeremiah 39:11.text: I took the purchase document, the sealed one and the one that had been read.

Jeremiah 39:12.text: I gave it to Baruch son of Neriah son of Maaseiah, before Hanamel my father’s brother’s son, before those standing there and writing in the purchase document, and before the Judeans in the prison court.

Jeremiah 39:13.text: Before their eyes I instructed Baruch:

Jeremiah 39:14.text: Thus said the Lord Almighty: Take this purchase document and the document that has been read, and put it in an earthenware vessel so that it may last many days.

Jeremiah 39:15.text: For thus said the Lord: Fields, houses, and vineyards will again be acquired in this land.

Jeremiah 39:16.text: After giving the purchase document to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the Lord:

Jeremiah 39:17.text: O Lord, Thou madest heaven and earth by Thy great strength and Thy high, uplifted arm. Nothing can be hidden from Thee.

Jeremiah 39:18.text: Thou showest mercy to thousands and repayest fathers’ sins into their children’s laps after them, the great and strong God,

Jeremiah 39:19.text: Lord of great counsel and powerful in works, the great God, the Almighty and renowned Lord. Thine eyes are upon the ways of human beings, to give each according to his way.

Jeremiah 39:20.text: Thou didst perform signs and wonders in Egypt down to this day, in Israel and among earthborn people, and madest a name for Thyself as it is this day.

Jeremiah 39:21.text: Thou broughtest Thy people Israel out of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a mighty hand, a high arm, and great sights.

Jeremiah 39:22.text: Thou gavest them this land, which Thou hadst sworn to their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.

Jeremiah 39:23.text: They entered and received it, but did not obey Thy voice or walk in Thine ordinances. They did none of all that Thou didst command them, and Thou didst cause all these calamities to befall them.

Jeremiah 39:24.text: A multitude has reached this city to seize it. The city was handed over to the Chaldeans fighting it because of sword and famine. As Thou spakest, so it happened.

Jeremiah 39:25.text: Yet Thou sayest to me, Acquire a field with silver. And I wrote a document, sealed it, and called witnesses—even though the city was handed over to the Chaldeans.

Jeremiah 39:26.text: The Lord’s word came to me:

Jeremiah 39:27.text: I am the Lord, the God of all flesh. Can anything be hidden from Me?

Jeremiah 39:28.text: Therefore thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: This city will certainly be handed over to Babylon’s king, and he will take it.

Jeremiah 39:29.text: The Chaldeans fighting this city will come and burn this city with fire. They will burn down the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to Baal and poured libations to other gods to provoke Me bitterly.

Jeremiah 39:30.text: The children of Israel and Judah alone were doing evil in My sight from their youth.

Jeremiah 39:31.text: This city has aroused My anger and wrath from the day they built it until this day, so that I would remove it from My presence,

Jeremiah 39:32.text: because of all the wicked deeds the children of Israel and Judah committed to embitter Me—they and their kings, their rulers, their priests, their prophets, the men of Judah and Jerusalem’s inhabitants.

Jeremiah 39:33.text: They turned their backs to Me, not their faces. I taught them from early morning and kept teaching, but they did not listen and take hold of discipline.

Jeremiah 39:34.text: They set their pollutions in the house over which My name is invoked, amid their impurities.

Jeremiah 39:35.text: They built the altars to Baal in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, to offer their sons and daughters to Molech the king. I had not instructed them, nor had it entered My heart, to do this abomination and cause Judah to sin.

Jeremiah 39:36.text: And now, thus said the Lord, Israel’s God, concerning the city of which you say, It will be handed over to Babylon’s king by sword, famine, and a sent affliction:

Jeremiah 39:37.text: I am gathering them from all the land where I scattered them in My anger, wrath, and great indignation. I will bring them back to this place and settle them in confidence.

Jeremiah 39:38.text: They will be My people, and I will be their God.

Jeremiah 39:39.text: I will give them another way and another heart, to fear Me always, for their good and their children’s good after them.

Jeremiah 39:40.text: I will establish an eternal covenant with them, which I will certainly not turn back from behind them. I will put My fear in their heart so that they do not depart from Me.

Jeremiah 39:41.text: I will attend to them to do them good and will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all heart and all soul.

Jeremiah 39:42.text: For thus said the Lord: Just as I brought all these great calamities upon this people, so I will bring upon them all the good things I spoke concerning them.

Jeremiah 39:43.text: Fields will again be acquired in the land of which you say, It is untrodden by people and animals, and they were handed over to the Chaldeans.

Jeremiah 39:44.text: They will acquire fields with silver, and you will write a document, seal it, and call witnesses in Benjamin’s land, around Jerusalem, in Judah’s cities, the hill-country cities, the cities of the Shephelah, and the cities of the Negeb, because I will bring back their exiles.

Jeremiah 40:1.text: The Lord’s word came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still bound in the prison court:

Jeremiah 40:2.text: Thus said the Lord, who makes the earth and forms it to set it upright—the Lord is His name:

Jeremiah 40:3.text: Cry out to Me and I will answer you. I will announce to you great, mighty things you have not known.

Jeremiah 40:4.text: For thus said the Lord, Israel’s God, about this city’s houses and the houses of Judah’s king, torn down for siegeworks and defenses,

Jeremiah 40:5.text: to fight the Chaldeans and fill the city with the dead bodies of people I struck in My anger and wrath. I turned My face from them because of all their wicked deeds.

Jeremiah 40:6.text: I am bringing her the closing of wounds and a remedy. I will reveal to them that I listen, heal her, and make peace and faithfulness for them.

Jeremiah 40:7.text: I will bring back Judah’s exiles and Israel’s exiles and build them as before.

Jeremiah 40:8.text: I will cleanse them from all the injustices by which they sinned against Me. I will certainly not remember the sins they committed against Me when they departed from Me.

Jeremiah 40:9.text: It will be for joy, praise, and greatness to all the people of the earth. They will hear all the good things I will do, and they will fear and be distressed over all the good and peace I will bring them.

Jeremiah 40:10.text: Thus said the Lord: Again in this place, which you call deserted of people and animals, in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem, desolate because there are no people or animals, there will be heard

Jeremiah 40:11.text: the sound of joy and rejoicing, the bridegroom’s voice and the bride’s voice, the voices of those saying, Give thanks to the Lord Almighty, for the Lord is good; His mercy is for ever. They will bring gifts into the Lord’s house, for I will bring back all the exiles of that land as before, said the Lord.

Jeremiah 40:12.text: Thus said the Lord of forces: Again in this place, deserted because there are no people or animals, and in all its cities, there will be lodgings for shepherds settling sheep down.

Jeremiah 40:13.text: In the hill-country cities, the cities of the Shephelah, the cities of the Negeb, in Benjamin’s land, in the places around Jerusalem, and in Judah’s cities, sheep will again pass under the hand of the one counting, said the Lord.

2 Kings 23:34.text: Pharaoh Nechao made Eliakim, son of Josiah king of Judah, king over them in place of his father Josiah and changed his name to Joakim. He took Joachas and brought him into Egypt, and he died there.

2 Kings 23:35.text: Joakim gave the silver and gold to Pharaoh, but assessed the land to provide the silver at Pharaoh’s command. Each according to his assessment, they gave the silver and gold with the people of the land, to give to Pharaoh Nechao.

2 Kings 23:36.text: Joakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jeldaph daughter of Phedeia, from Rouma.

2 Kings 23:33.text: Pharaoh Nechao removed him at Deblatha in Emath’s land so that he would not reign in Jerusalem. He imposed a penalty on the land of one hundred talents of silver and one hundred talents of gold.

2 Kings 23:37.text: He did what was evil in the Lord’s eyes, according to everything his fathers had done.

Jeremiah 7:2.text: Hear the Lord’s word, all Judea!

Jeremiah 7:3.text: Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Correct your ways and your practices, and I will settle you in this place.

Jeremiah 6:30.text: Call them rejected silver, because the Lord rejected them.

Jeremiah 7:4.text: Do not put your confidence in yourselves on false words, because they will not benefit you at all when they say, ‘The Lord’s temple, the Lord’s temple it is.’

Deuteronomy 4:2.text: You shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall you take away from it; you shall keep the commandments of the Lord your God, which I command you this day.

Deuteronomy 4:1.text: And now, O Israel, hear the ordinances and the judgments which I teach you this day to do, that you may live and be multiplied, and enter and inherit the land which the Lord, the God of your fathers, gives you.

Deuteronomy 4:3.text: Your eyes have seen all that the Lord our God did unto Baal-peor; for every man who went after Baal-peor, the Lord your God blotted him out from among you.

Jeremiah 7:23.text: But this utterance I commanded them, saying: Hear My voice, and I will be your God and you will be My people; and walk in all My ways that I command you, so that it may be well with you.

Jeremiah 7:22.text: For I did not speak to your fathers or command them on the day I brought them up from Egypt’s land concerning whole burnt offerings and sacrifice.

Jeremiah 22:16.text: They did not know; they did not judge a case for the lowly or a case for the poor. Is this not your failing to know Me? says the Lord.

Jeremiah 22:17.text: Behold, neither your eyes nor your heart are good; instead they are directed toward your greed, innocent blood to shed it, wrongdoing, and murder to commit it.

Jeremiah 22:18.text: Therefore thus says the Lord concerning Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: Woe upon this man! They will certainly not mourn him, O brother! Nor will they weep for him, Alas, lord!

Jeremiah 22:19.text: He will be buried with a donkey’s burial; swept up, he will be thrown beyond Jerusalem’s gate.

Jeremiah 22:20.text: Go up to Lebanon and cry out; raise your voice in Bashan and shout to the far side of the sea, because all your lovers have been shattered.

Jeremiah 22:21.text: I spoke to you in your falling away, and you said, I will not listen. This is your way from your youth: you did not hear My voice.

Jeremiah 22:22.text: Wind will shepherd all your shepherds, and your lovers will go out in captivity. Then you will be ashamed and dishonored because of all who love you.

Jeremiah 22:23.text: You who dwell in Lebanon and nest among the cedars will groan when pangs come upon you like those of a woman giving birth.

Jeremiah 22:24.text: As I live, says the Lord, even if Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, becomes a signet on My right hand, I will pull you off from there,

Jeremiah 22:25.text: and hand you into the hands of those seeking your life, those before whom you are afraid, into the hands of the Chaldeans.

Jeremiah 22:26.text: And I will cast you and your mother who bore you into a land where you were not born, and there you both will die.

Jeremiah 22:27.text: But to the land for which they pray in their souls, they will certainly not return.

Jeremiah 22:28.text: Jeconiah was dishonored like a vessel for which there is no use, because he was cast out and thrown into a land he did not know.

Jeremiah 22:29.text: Land, land, hear the Lord’s word:

Jeremiah 22:30.text: Record this man as an outcast, because no man from his offspring will grow great sitting on David’s throne and ruling again in Judah.

Jeremiah 23:1.text: O shepherds who scatter and destroy the sheep of My pasture!

Jeremiah 23:2.text: Therefore thus says the Lord to those shepherding My people: You scattered My sheep and drove them out without visiting them. Behold, I am exacting justice from you according to your evil practices.

Jeremiah 23:3.text: And I will receive the remnant of My people from all the land where I drove them out, and establish them in their pasture; they will increase and multiply.

Jeremiah 23:4.text: And I will raise shepherds for them who will tend them, and they will no longer fear or be frightened, says the Lord.

Jeremiah 23:5.text: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will raise up a righteous rising for David. A king will reign and understand, doing judgment and righteousness upon the earth.

Jeremiah 23:6.text: In his days Judah will be saved and Israel will dwell confidently. This is his name, which the Lord will call him: Josedek.

Jeremiah 23:7.text: Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and they will no longer say, As the Lord lives, who brought Israel’s house up from Egypt’s land,

Jeremiah 23:8.text: but, As the Lord lives, who gathered all Israel’s offspring from the northern land and all the countries where He drove them out, and restored them to their land.

Jeremiah 23:9.text: Among the prophets my heart was shattered; within me all my bones were shaken. I became like a shattered man, like a person gripped by wine, before the Lord and the splendor of His glory.

Jeremiah 23:10.text: Because of these things the land mourned and the wilderness pastures dried up. Their course became evil, and their strength was not so.

Jeremiah 23:11.text: Because priest and prophet were defiled, and in My house I saw their evils.

Jeremiah 23:12.text: Therefore let their way become a slippery place for them in darkness, and they will be tripped and fall in it, because I will bring evils upon them in their year of visitation, says the Lord.

Jeremiah 23:13.text: And among Samaria’s prophets I saw lawless acts: they prophesied through Baal and led My people Israel astray.

Jeremiah 23:14.text: And among Jerusalem’s prophets I have seen horrifying things: committing adultery, walking in lies, and supporting evil hands so that no one turns from his evil way. They all became like Sodom to Me, and her inhabitants like Gomorrah.

Jeremiah 23:15.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will feed them pain and give them bitter water to drink, because from Jerusalem’s prophets defilement went out into all the land.

Jeremiah 23:16.text: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Do not listen to the prophets’ words, because they make a vision futile for themselves. They speak from their own heart and not from the Lord’s mouth.

Jeremiah 23:17.text: They say to those rejecting the Lord’s word, You will have peace. To all who walk according to their own wishes, to everyone walking in the wandering of his heart, they said, No evils will come upon you.

Jeremiah 23:18.text: Because who stood in the Lord’s standing place and saw His word? Who gave ear and heard?

Jeremiah 23:19.text: Behold, a shaking comes from the Lord, and anger goes out into a convulsion; swirling, it will come upon the ungodly.

Jeremiah 23:20.text: And the Lord’s fury will no longer turn back until He does it and raises it up from His heart’s undertaking. At the end of the days they will understand these things.

Jeremiah 23:21.text: I was not sending the prophets, yet they ran; I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied.

Jeremiah 23:22.text: And if they had stood in My standing presence and listened to My words, they would have turned My people from their evil practices.

Jeremiah 23:23.text: I am a God drawing near, says the Lord, and not a God far away.

Jeremiah 23:24.text: If a person hides in hidden places, will I not see him? Do I not fill the heaven and the earth? says the Lord.

Jeremiah 23:25.text: I heard what the prophets speak, the false things they prophesy in My name, saying, I dreamed a dream.

Jeremiah 23:26.text: How long will it be in the heart of the prophets prophesying false things, and in their prophesying the wishes of their own heart?

Jeremiah 23:27.text: They plan to forget My law through their dreams, which each told his neighbor, just as their fathers forgot My name through Baal.

Jeremiah 23:28.text: Let the prophet in whom there is a dream tell his dream, and the one to whom My word comes tell My word in truth. What has chaff to do with wheat? So are My words, says the Lord.

Jeremiah 23:29.text: Are not My words like blazing fire, says the Lord, and like an axe cutting rock?

Jeremiah 23:30.text: Therefore behold, I am against the prophets, says the Lord God, who steal My words, each from his neighbor.

Jeremiah 23:31.text: Behold, I am against the prophets who cast out prophecies of the tongue and doze their own dozing.

Jeremiah 23:32.text: Behold, I am against the prophets who prophesy false dreams, who told them and led My people astray by their lies and wanderings. I did not send or command them, and they will bring this people no benefit at all.

Jeremiah 23:33.text: And if this people, a priest, or a prophet asks you, What is the Lord’s burden? say to them, You are the burden, and I will dash you down, says the Lord.

Jeremiah 23:34.text: And the prophet, priest, or people who say, The Lord’s burden—I will exact justice from that person and his household.

Jeremiah 23:35.text: For this is what you will say, each to his neighbor and his brother: What did the Lord answer? What did the Lord speak?

Jeremiah 23:36.text: And do not name the Lord’s burden again, because a person’s own word will be his burden.

Jeremiah 23:37.text: And why did the Lord our God speak?

Jeremiah 23:38.text: Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you said this word, The Lord’s burden, though I sent to you saying, Do not say The Lord’s burden,

Jeremiah 23:39.text: therefore behold, I seize you and dash you down, along with the city I gave to you and your fathers,

Jeremiah 23:40.text: and I will put eternal reproach and eternal dishonor upon you, which will not be forgotten.

Jeremiah 24:1.text: The Lord showed me two baskets of figs lying before the Lord’s sanctuary, after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had deported Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, the rulers, craftsmen, prisoners, and rich people from Jerusalem and brought them to Babylon.

Jeremiah 24:2.text: One basket had very good figs, like early figs; the other basket had very bad figs that could not be eaten because of their badness.

Jeremiah 24:3.text: And the Lord said to me: What do you see, Jeremiah? I said: Figs. The good are exceedingly good, and the bad exceedingly bad; they cannot be eaten because of their badness.

Jeremiah 24:4.text: And the Lord’s word came to me, saying:

Jeremiah 24:5.text: Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Like these good figs, so I will acknowledge Judah’s deportees, whom I have sent from this place to the Chaldeans’ land, for good things.

Jeremiah 24:6.text: And I will fix My eyes upon them for good things and restore them to this land for good things. I will rebuild them and certainly not tear them down, plant them and certainly not pluck them out.

Jeremiah 24:7.text: And I will give them a heart to know Me, that I am the Lord. They will be My people and I will be their God, because they will return to Me from their whole heart.

Jeremiah 24:8.text: And like the bad figs that cannot be eaten because of their badness—thus says the Lord—so I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah, his nobles, Jerusalem’s remnant left in this land, and those dwelling in Egypt.

Jeremiah 24:9.text: And I will give them to scattering into all the earth’s kingdoms, and they will become a reproach, a parable, an object of hatred, and a curse in every place where I drove them out.

Jeremiah 24:10.text: And I will send famine, death, and sword against them until they disappear from the land I gave them.

Isaiah 60:20.text: For your sun will not set, and your moon will not fail. The Lord will be your everlasting light, and your days of mourning will be fulfilled.

Isaiah 60:21.text: Your people will all be righteous, and they will inherit the land for ever, guarding the planting, the works of His hands, for glory.

Isaiah 60:22.text: The fewest will become thousands, and the least a great nation. I, the Lord, will gather them at the proper time.

Jeremiah 6:13.text: For from their small to their great, all have carried out lawless deeds; from priest to false prophet, all have done false things.

Jeremiah 6:14.text: And they treated My people’s fracture with contempt, saying, ‘Peace, peace’; and where is peace?

Jeremiah 6:15.text: They were put to shame because they failed, and even so they were not at all ashamed and did not recognize their dishonor. Therefore they will fall in their fall, and at the time of their visitation they will perish, said the Lord.

Jeremiah 43:1.text: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, the Lord’s word came to me:

Jeremiah 43:2.text: Take a writing roll and write on it all the words I have delivered to you as oracles concerning Jerusalem, Judah, and all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah king of Judah until today.

Acts 6:8.text: Stephen, full of grace and power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people.

Acts 6:9.text: But some from the synagogue called the Freedmen’s, including Cyrenians and Alexandrians and people from Cilicia and Asia, rose up and disputed with Stephen.

Acts 6:10.text: They could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.

Micah 3:9.text: Hear these things now, leaders of Jacob’s house and remaining ones of Israel’s house, who abhor justice and twist all straight things,

Micah 3:10.text: you who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustices!

Jeremiah 47:7.text: All the commanders of the force in the countryside, they and their men, heard that Babylon’s king had appointed Gedaliah in the land and had entrusted to him men and their wives whom he had not deported to Babylon.

Jeremiah 47:12.text: They came to Gedaliah in Judah’s land at Mizpah and gathered a very great amount of wine and summer fruit, and oil.

Daniel 2:31.text: You, O king, saw a single image. That image was exceedingly large, its appearance was extraordinary as it stood before you, and the image’s appearance was frightening.

Daniel 2:32.text: Its head was good gold, its chest and arms silver, and its belly and thighs bronze,

Daniel 2:33.text: its legs iron, and its feet partly iron and partly earthenware.

Daniel 2:34.text: You watched until a stone was cut from a mountain without hands. It struck the image on its feet of iron and earthenware and ground them down.

Daniel 2:35.text: Then the iron, earthenware, bronze, silver, and gold were ground fine together, becoming finer than chaff on a threshing floor. The wind scattered them so that nothing remained of them. The stone that struck the image became a great mountain and struck the whole earth.

Hebrews 8:1.text: Now the main point in what is being said is this: we have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,

Hebrews 8:2.text: a minister of the holy places and of the true tent, which the Lord pitched, not a human being.

Hebrews 8:3.text: For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices; therefore this One too must have something to offer.

Hebrews 8:4.text: Now if He were on earth, He would not even be a priest, since there are those who offer the gifts according to law.

Hebrews 8:5.text: They serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, just as Moses was instructed when he was about to complete the tent. For He says, “See that you make everything according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.”

Hebrews 8:6.text: But now He has obtained a more excellent ministry, insofar as He is also mediator of a better covenant, which has been established as law upon better promises.

2 Corinthians 3:5.text: Not that we are sufficient in ourselves to consider anything as coming from ourselves, but our sufficiency is from God,

2 Corinthians 3:6.text: who also made us sufficient as ministers of a new covenant, not of letter but of Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

2 Corinthians 3:7.text: Now if the ministry of death, engraved in letters on stones, came in glory, so that the sons of Israel could not gaze at Moses’ face because of the glory of his face, which was being brought to an end,

2 Corinthians 3:8.text: how much more will the ministry of the Spirit be in glory?

Isaiah 48:3.text: I announced the former things beforehand; they went out from My mouth and were heard. Suddenly I acted, and they arrived.

Isaiah 48:4.text: I know that you are stubborn, your neck an iron sinew and your forehead bronze.

Isaiah 48:5.text: I announced it to you long ago; before it came upon you I made you hear it. Do not say, ‘My idols did it,’ or say, ‘My carved and cast images commanded me.’

Isaiah 48:6.text: You heard everything, but you did not understand. Yet I also made you hear the new things from now on, what is about to happen, and you did not speak.

Isaiah 48:7.text: They happen now, not long ago; you did not hear them in earlier days. Do not say, ‘Yes, I know them.’

Isaiah 48:8.text: You neither knew nor understood; from the beginning I did not open your ears. For I knew you would utterly reject faithfulness, and you would be called lawless even from the belly.

Jeremiah 6:8.text: you will be instructed, Jerusalem, lest My soul depart from you, lest I make you an impassable land that will not be inhabited.

Jeremiah 6:9.text: For thus says the Lord: Glean, glean Israel’s remnants like a vine; turn back like the grape-gatherer to his basket.

Jeremiah 6:10.text: To whom shall I speak and testify, and he will hear? Behold, their ears are uncircumcised, and they cannot hear. Behold, the Lord’s utterance became a reproach to them; they certainly will not wish to hear it.

Jeremiah 6:11.text: And I filled up My fury and held back and did not bring them to an end. I will pour it upon little children outside and upon a gathering of young men together, because man and woman will be seized, the elder with one full of days.

Jeremiah 6:12.text: And their houses will be transferred to others, fields and their wives together, because I will stretch out My hand against those dwelling in this land, says the Lord.

2 Kings 24:6.text: Joakim lay down with his fathers, and his son Joakim became king in his place.

2 Kings 24:7.text: The king of Egypt did not again leave his land, because the king of Babylon had taken everything belonging to the king of Egypt from Egypt’s torrent to the River Euphrates.

2 Kings 24:8.text: Joakim was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Nestha daughter of Ellanathan, from Jerusalem.

2 Kings 24:9.text: He did what was evil in the Lord’s eyes, according to everything his father had done.

2 Kings 24:10.text: At that time Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.

Isaiah 1:1.text: The vision that Isaiah son of Amos saw, which he saw against Judea and against Jerusalem during the reign of Oziah, Joatham, Achaz and Hezekiah, who reigned over Judea.
